raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

`get_lock` flattens the whole model path into the lock file name:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
model_name = model_name_or_path.replace("/", "-")
hash_name = hashlib.sha256(model_name.encode()).hexdigest()
# add hash to avoid conflict with old users' lock files
lock_file_name = hash_name + model_name + ".lock"
lock = filelock.FileLock(os.path.join(lock_dir, lock_file_name), mode=0o666)
```

The digest is 64 characters, so any `--model` path longer than roughly 186 characters produces a file **name** over the 255-byte cap that ext4, xfs, btrfs and APFS all put on a single path component. The full *path* may be far longer than 255 bytes, which is why this is easy to miss — the limit is per component.

It only bites on local checkpoint paths, but it bites before a single weight is read:

```
OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long
```

Reproduced on a 221-character local checkpoint path, which lands the lock name at 290 bytes:

```python
>>> path = ("/mnt/shared-storage/models/team-inference/experiments/"
...         "2026-02-long-context-run-17/checkpoints/global_step_120000/"
...         "hf_export/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8-blockwise/snapshot/"
...         "revision-2026-02-14-rc3-merged-lora-adapters/final")
>>> get_lock(path, cache_dir=tmpdir)
OSError errno=63: File name too long          # ENAMETOOLONG, macOS numbering
```

`get_lock` guards the weight download, the config download and the tokenizer download — 8 call sites in `weight_utils.py` and `tokenizers/registry.py` — so this takes out model loading entirely for anyone serving from a deep shared-storage or multi-revision export path.

## Changes

Fall back to the digest alone when the composed name is too long:

```python
if len(os.fsencode(lock_file_name)) > 255:
    lock_file_name = hash_name + ".lock"
```

The digest is already collision-resistant and is derived from the same string, so the lock stays per-model. Ordinary Hugging Face model ids keep their existing lock file name — that matters, because the file name is what makes the lock shared between processes, and changing it unconditionally would let two concurrent vLLM processes download the same model at once.

This is the same fix that already shipped in SGLang's fork of this function (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/weight_utils.py`), which is where I noticed the divergence.

## Test

`tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py::test_get_lock_handles_long_model_paths`, parametrized over a normal model id and the long path above. It asserts the basename stays within 255 bytes and that the lock can actually be acquired.

On current `main`:

```
FAILED tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py::test_get_lock_handles_long_model_paths[/mnt/shared-storage/...]
1 failed, 1 passed
```

With this PR, the whole file passes:

```
$ pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py
34 passed in 41.07s
```

No GPU needed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both changed files.

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure was reproduced against current `main`, and the new test was run both with and without the fix. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

files.patch:
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
 
+import os
 import tempfile
 from unittest.mock import Mock
 
@@ -11,6 +12,7 @@
 from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.weight_utils import (
     download_weights_from_hf,
     drop_checkpoint_cache,
+    get_lock,
     maybe_remap_kv_scale_name,
 )
 
@@ -309,3 +311,33 @@ def test_drop_checkpoint_cache_releases_local_weight_files(
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     test_download_weights_from_hf()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "model_name_or_path",
+    [
+        "facebook/opt-125m",
+        # A local checkpoint path flattened into the lock file name. 221
+        # characters here, which lands the name at 290 bytes once the 64-char
+        # digest and the ".lock" suffix are added.
+        (
+            "/mnt/shared-storage/models/team-inference/experiments/"
+            "2026-02-long-context-run-17/checkpoints/global_step_120000/"
+            "hf_export/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8-blockwise/snapshot/"
+            "revision-2026-02-14-rc3-merged-lora-adapters/final"
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_get_lock_handles_long_model_paths(model_name_or_path: str):
+    """The lock file name has to stay inside the filesystem's limit.
+
+    A single path component is capped at 255 bytes on the common Linux
+    filesystems (and on macOS), while the full path may be much longer, so a
+    long ``--model`` path used to raise ``OSError: File name too long`` before
+    any weights were touched.
+    """
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
+        lock = get_lock(model_name_or_path, cache_dir=os.path.join(tmpdir, "locks"))
+        assert len(os.fsencode(os.path.basename(lock.lock_file))) <= 255
+        with lock:
+            assert os.path.exists(lock.lock_file)

@@ -96,6 +96,13 @@ def get_lock(model_name_or_path: str | Path, cache_dir: str | None = None):
     hash_name = hashlib.sha256(model_name.encode()).hexdigest()
     # add hash to avoid conflict with old users' lock files
     lock_file_name = hash_name + model_name + ".lock"
+    # Most filesystems cap a single path component at 255 bytes even though the
+    # full path may be far longer, and a local checkpoint path flattened into
+    # the name blows past that (`OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long`).
+    # The digest already identifies the model, so fall back to it alone and
+    # keep the historical name for ordinary model ids.
+    if len(os.fsencode(lock_file_name)) > 255:
+        lock_file_name = hash_name + ".lock"
     # mode 0o666 is required for the filelock to be shared across users
     lock = filelock.FileLock(os.path.join(lock_dir, lock_file_name), mode=0o666)
     return lock
